meta.title: Animals: how big they were | Museum of Ages
meta.description: How big the museum's animals were, each beside a person 1.70 m tall to one scale, in our own pictures with their sources.

top.answer: The museum is building a wing of animals, from the giants of long ago to the last of their kind. Until it opens, each page here answers one question: how big was this animal? Our own picture puts it beside a person of 1.70 m, to one scale, with the numbers and what they rest on.

out.text: Museum of Ages is a digital museum. Open today is the Leonardo da Vinci wing. Free entry, no account.

items.alt: Our megalodon from the side, about 16 m (52 ft) long, mouth closed, dark grey with a paler band along the flank, beside a grey person 1.70 m tall who looks tiny next to it.

Our seven dinosaurs in a row from the side, to one scale. The longest, our Argentinosaurus, is about 30.6 m (100 ft), two long necks tower over the rest, and a grey person 1.70 m tall looks tiny beside them.
Our T. rex from the side on two legs, about 11.4 m (37 ft) long in this pose, mouth closed and head raised, beside a grey person 1.70 m tall who stands far below its hips.

Our young Spinosaurus from the side, about 10 m (33 ft) long, with a tall sail and a deep tail. Behind it the pale outline of the largest adults, just under 14 m (46 ft) by a model, and beside it a grey person 1.70 m tall who reaches its hip.

Our woolly mammoth, the Berezovka bull, from the side in a dark brown coat: high domed head, sloping back, two curved tusks, and a mark at his shoulder, 271 cm (8.9 ft) by a reconstruction. The grey person beside him, 1.70 m tall, stands lower than the tusk tips.

Our Brachiosaurus from the side, built at the Chicago skeleton's size, 24.0 m (79 ft) along the backbone, its long neck raised in a gentle curve to a head top 11.5 m (38 ft) up, the neck angle our choice. The front legs are longer than the hind legs, the tail is off the ground, and a grey person 1.70 m tall could walk under its belly.

Our Triceratops from the side, 6.9 m (23 ft) from beak to tail and 2.5 m (8 ft) high over the hips: a wide frill behind the head, two long horns over the eyes, a short one on the nose, four legs. Beside it a grey person 1.70 m tall who reaches about two thirds of the way up its back.

Our Ankylosaurus from the side, 6.4 m (21 ft) from beak to club, its back 1.7 m (5.6 ft) high over the hips: a low, wide body under rows of bony plates, a broad head carried low, four short legs and a straight tail ending in a flat club. Beside it a grey person 1.70 m tall, as tall as the top of its back.

Our Stegosaurus from the side, 5.6 m (18 ft) from beak to tail tip, its back 1.9 m (6.4 ft) high over the hips: a small low head, two rows of tall plates along the arched back, two of its four tail spikes, the front legs shorter than the hind legs. Beside it a grey person 1.70 m tall whose head stays below the top of its back.

Our blue whale from the side, 22.86 m (75 ft) long: a slim blue-grey body with pale mottling, a flat head, a long, pale-edged flipper and a small back fin far back. Beside it a grey person 1.70 m tall who reaches a little past halfway up its side.
